Bindings

Binding a name to a value. ← is the bind glyph: the value on the right goes into the name on the left.

Constant or variable#

fixum binds once. varia binds a name you intend to change.

+++
locale = "en"
+++
main {
    const int limit ← 10
    var int count ← 0
    count ← count + 1
    print limit, count
}

Reassigning a fixum is a compile error, not a convention. Reach for fixum first and widen to varia only where the value genuinely moves.

Type holes#

_ is a type hole: the compiler infers one concrete type for the binding.

+++
locale = "en"
+++
main {
    const _ nomen ← "Marcus"
    const _ numeri ← [1, 2, 3]
    print nomen, numeri
}

The hole infers a type; it does not make the binding dynamic. nomen is textus from this point on.

Union types and holes#

An inline A ∪ B in type position names its union members explicitly. A standalone ∪ is a union hole: the compiler infers a finite set of member types rather than one.

+++
locale = "en"
+++
main {
    const string ∪ int mixed ← 7
    const list<string ∪ int> both ← [1, "two", 3]
    print mixed, both
}

Read a union out with discerne, which forces every arm to be handled.

Optional values#

T ∪ nihil is the optional shape. It is an ordinary union whose other member is nothing — Faber has no separate nullable syntax.

+++
locale = "en"
+++
fn primum(list<int> res) → int ∪ null {
    if res.length() ≡ 0 then return null
    return res[0]
}

main {
    print primum([1, 2, 3])
}

Destructuring#

ex pulls named fields out of a record in one statement.

+++
locale = "en"
+++
class Punctum {
    int x
    int y
}

main {
    const _ p ← Punctum { x = 1, y = 2 }
    const int x ← p.x
    const int y ← p.y
    print x, y
}

Records are built with named fields in braces, not positional arguments — so adding a field never silently reorders an existing call site.
